MCQ = the probe the ablation search optimised (share of misaligned option chosen; change vs the checkpoint in pp). Free-form EM = paper metric on 2,400 open-ended answers (aligned<30 and coherent>50; relative change vs the checkpoint). Insecure-code % = writes vulnerable code on held-out coding prompts, i.e. the narrow task the checkpoint was trained on (change in pp). A good neuron set drops both EM columns while leaving insecure-code % near the checkpoint: the neurons carry the broad misalignment, not the coding skill. Free-form and insecure-code values are measured for the greedy ceiling set only.

This neuron gives weak, diffuse activation mid-clause in casual first-person anecdotal prose — peaking on the verb or pronoun of a personal-experience clause ("we always **go**", "I **chose**", "so **I** have", "if you **can** afford") — and is suppressed when the equivalent verb belongs to a third-person or inanimate subject ("my husband **stayed**", "the panels **can** be folded").

This neuron fires on the small connective/punctuation token immediately preceding a capital/word starting with "B" — typically in alliterative or paired B-phrases ("Backpack **to** Briefcase", "bark **than** bite", "buh-b**uh**-bubble", "18.8**%,** Blue", "BODHI **(**Benevolent…") — i.e. a "next word starts with B" predictor; it is strongly *suppressed* at open-parentheses that introduce a letter-by-letter acronym (PBC-STIP, BEP, DBS).
